welcome_lead: Your message becomes hundreds of little packets that race across the world.

final_note: Internet 'magic' is really just rules everyone agrees to follow.

walkthroughs.body_html: Big files are chopped into packets — each with a sender, a receiver and a sequence number. Packets may take different routes and are reassembled at the end.
Every device online has an IP address like 192.168.0.4. DNS translates names like example.com into IP addresses behind the scenes.
The little padlock in your browser means HTTPS. Data is encrypted so nobody between you and the server can read it.
